about: Candidate pool and multi-word questions for rank(). Each question lists what the two retrievers return for it (semantic: [id, cosine similarity] best first, as olo_match gives; keyword: [id, ts_rank] best first, as olo_search_text gives, after the loose retry when the strict query found nothing). expect_top must all be in the top k; forbid_top must not be. fails_before marks the cases plain fusion (fuse) gets wrong. The atoms are written for this test, modelled on real Commons records; urls are examples.

atoms.title: Coral reef
atoms.summary: Coral reefs are underwater ecosystems built by colonies of coral polyps held together by calcium carbonate. They cover less than one percent of the ocean floor yet shelter about a quarter of marine species.

atoms.title: Coral bleaching
atoms.summary: When water stays too warm, corals expel the algae living in their tissues and turn white. Bleached corals are not dead but starve and become prone to disease.

atoms.title: Recovery of coral reefs after mass bleaching events
atoms.summary: Long term surveys show reefs can recover within ten to fifteen years after bleaching when local fishing pressure and pollution are low and larvae arrive from connected reefs.

atoms.title: Recovery of coral reefs after mass bleaching events
atoms.summary: Long term surveys show reefs can recover within ten to fifteen years after bleaching when local fishing pressure and pollution are low and larvae arrive from connected reefs.

atoms.title: Reef fish diversity
atoms.summary: Reef fish are the most diverse vertebrates on coral reefs, with several thousand species in the Indo Pacific alone.

atoms.title: Ocean acidification
atoms.summary: The ocean absorbs about a quarter of the carbon dioxide people emit, lowering its pH and making it harder for corals and shellfish to build skeletons.

atoms.title: Great Barrier Reef
atoms.summary: The world's largest coral reef system, off Queensland, Australia, made of nearly three thousand individual reefs.

atoms.title: Gutenberg Bible
atoms.summary: The Gutenberg Bible was the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type. Gutenberg's workshop printed about 180 copies of the Gutenberg Bible in Mainz.

atoms.title: Johannes Gutenberg
atoms.summary: Johannes Gutenberg was a German goldsmith and printer. Gutenberg introduced movable type printing to Europe around 1440.

atoms.title: Project Gutenberg ebook catalogue
atoms.summary: Machine readable catalogue of the Project Gutenberg collection in RDF and CSV, updated weekly.

atoms.title: Project Gutenberg
atoms.summary: A volunteer effort to digitise and archive cultural works, founded in 1971 by Michael Hart. It is the oldest digital library.

atoms.title: Open data projects
atoms.summary: A list of community projects that publish open data under free licences.

atoms.title: Printing press
atoms.summary: A device that applies pressure to an inked surface resting on paper, spreading printed books across Europe from the fifteenth century.

atoms.title: Microplastics in the ocean
atoms.summary: Fragments of plastic smaller than five millimetres are found from the surface to the deep sea floor.

atoms.title: Health effects of microplastic exposure in humans
atoms.summary: A review of the evidence on how ingested and inhaled microplastics affect human health, including inflammation and the uncertainty in current measurements.

atoms.title: Air pollution and human health
atoms.summary: Fine particles in polluted air raise the risk of heart and lung disease; the WHO estimates millions of early deaths a year.

atoms.title: Plastic recycling
atoms.summary: Only a small share of plastic waste is recycled; most is landfilled, burned or leaks into the environment.

atoms.title: Photosynthesis
atoms.summary: The process by which plants, algae and some bacteria use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugars and release oxygen.

atoms.title: Chlorophyll
atoms.summary: The green pigment in plants that absorbs light, mostly blue and red.

atoms.title: Solar power: turning sunlight into electricity
atoms.summary: Photovoltaic panels and concentrated solar plants convert the energy in sunlight into electric power.

atoms.title: Food security
atoms.summary: Food security means that all people at all times have access to enough safe and nutritious food.

atoms.title: Sea level rise
atoms.summary: Global mean sea level has risen about 20 centimetres since 1900, caused mainly by thermal expansion of warming sea water and melting glaciers and ice sheets.

atoms.title: Arctic sea ice decline
atoms.summary: Arctic sea ice in September has shrunk by about thirteen percent per decade since satellite records began in 1979.

atoms.title: Global temperature rise
atoms.summary: The Earth's surface is about 1.2 degrees warmer than before industrialisation, caused by greenhouse gases.

atoms.title: Tides
atoms.summary: Tides are the daily rise and fall of sea level caused by the pull of the Moon and the Sun.

atoms.title: Retreat of glaciers since 1850
atoms.summary: Mountain glaciers worldwide are shrinking. Glacier melt causes about a fifth of current sea level rise and threatens water supplies; the rise in glacier melt has accelerated since the 1990s as the level of warming grew.

atoms.title: MMR vaccine
atoms.summary: A combined vaccine against measles, mumps and rubella. Common side effects are fever, a mild rash and a sore arm; serious reactions are rare.

atoms.title: Vaccine
atoms.summary: A biological preparation that trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen.

atoms.title: Adverse drug reaction
atoms.summary: Harmful, unintended side effects of a medicine taken at a normal dose.

atoms.title: Measles
atoms.summary: A highly contagious viral disease that causes fever and a rash, preventable by vaccination.

atoms.title: Python (genus)
atoms.summary: Python is a genus of constricting snakes. The reticulated python and the Burmese python are among the longest snakes; python species live in Africa and Asia.

atoms.title: List of programming languages
atoms.summary: An alphabetical list of notable programming languages, from ABAP to Zig.

atoms.title: Python (programming language)
atoms.summary: A high level, general purpose programming language whose design emphasises readable syntax and significant indentation.

atoms.title: List comprehension
atoms.summary: A syntactic construct for building a list from an existing list, written in Python as [expression for item in iterable if condition].

atoms.title: Penicillin
atoms.summary: The first widely used antibiotic, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 when mould killed bacteria on a culture plate.

atoms.title: Alexander Fleming
atoms.summary: Scottish physician and microbiologist who discovered penicillin; he shared the 1945 Nobel Prize.

atoms.title: Antimicrobial resistance
atoms.summary: Bacteria that survive antibiotics spread resistance genes, making common infections harder to treat.
